articles.title: High salt diets disrupt the gut microbiome and impair memory in mice
articles.summary: A recent study found that both high-salt and severely low-salt diets impair memory in mice. While high salt triggers inflammation, extreme salt restriction starves the gut microbiome of metabolic byproducts needed for optimal brain function.

articles.summary: arXiv:2609.31792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform strongly on manipulation tasks, their responses to invalid task premises remain underexplored. articles.title: Replay in the Silent Degrees of Freedom: Continual Learning Without an Offline Phase
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.31630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Replay-based continual learning almost always consolidates in a dedicated offline phase or by interleaving replayed samples with the input stream, whereas brains also consolidate during wakefulness through local sleep, brief use-dependent off-periods of individual circuits. We ask whether a network trained by local, biologically constrained rules can consolidate with no offline phase at all. articles.summary: arXiv:2609.31631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models enable efficient scaling of large language models but face critical deployment challenges due to massive memory requirements. articles.title: Maternal psychopathic traits predict teens’ callous-unemotional traits a year later
articles.summary: A mother's emotional coldness may be a family risk marker for callous traits in teens with serious behavior problems. New research suggests the emotional side of maternal psychopathy predicts teens' callousness a year later, beyond their starting levels.

articles.title: Desk setups that encourage an expansive posture may boost risk-taking
articles.summary: A new study finds that environments forcing people into an upright posture—like a high desk—can subtly boost their willingness to take risks and feelings of pride, even without them realizing their posture was manipulated.

articles.summary: A recent psychology experiment shows that taking a few minutes to watch hopeful, goal-oriented YouTube videos can temporarily reduce feelings of depression and boost personal motivation.

articles.title: Towards a full-stack functionalist theory of consciousness: Identifying its functional profile
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.33366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: If consciousness is functional, a basic question is what awareness of a content actually changes in how a system operates on it. We ask, for a particular content X and mental or bodily process Y, whether awareness of X changes whether, or how well, X can be used in process Y. articles.title: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
articles.summary: A new study suggests coffee may influence mood and brain function by changing the activity of microbes in the gut. Both caffeinated and decaf coffee were linked to lower stress, depression, and impulsivity, while also producing measurable changes in gut bacteria and metabolites. Decaf was associated with better learning and memory, while caffeinated coffee appeared to reduce anxiety and improve attention.

articles.title: Psychological resilience may buffer children’s brains against some effects of abuse
articles.summary: New brain imaging research suggests resilience matters for children who have been abused. Among less resilient kids, abuse was tied to stronger links between emotional and bodily brain networks, which in turn tracked with more physical symptoms and depression.

articles.title: Faces and bodies send matching signals of attractiveness, but voices tell a different story
articles.summary: A recent study shows that a person's facial and bodily attractiveness are closely linked in the eyes of observers. However, the human voice operates independently, sending a separate biological message to potential partners.

articles.title: As America shifted left under Trump, emotional hostility widened the partisan gap
articles.summary: During Donald Trump’s first presidency, American public opinion broadly shifted leftward. But a new study reveals this "liberal rebound" was accompanied by surging emotional hostility between political parties, driving voters further apart on key policy issues.

articles.title: Brain structure linked to how well patients respond to an antidepressant, small study finds
articles.summary: Why do some people with depression respond to medication while others don't? A small study points to the brain's outer layer, finding that the folding complexity and thickness of certain cortical regions tracked how much patients improved.
